summary:
OMNITECH is an AI-powered, integrated astronaut health monitoring and mission support system designed to improve crew safety, autonomy, and decision-making during long-duration space missions, including future Mars exploration.

We developed four interconnected applications: OMNITECH PULSE, which monitors astronaut health indicators and identifies potential risks; OMNITECH COMMAND, which manages crew profiles, integrates mission data, and supports AI-assisted decisions; OMNITECH ORBIT, which provides planetary environmental monitoring and hazard awareness; and OMNITECH BEACON, which manages communications, emergency alerts, and information exchange.

Our solution addresses NASA's challenge by combining health monitoring, environmental awareness, intelligent risk assessment, and crew communication into one coordinated system. Its offline-first architecture, local AI capabilities, and secure networking design aim to support astronauts even when internet connectivity is limited or Earth communication is delayed.

Unlike conventional monitoring dashboards, OMNITECH is designed to transform collected information into understandable insights, early warnings, and actionable recommendations.

Our vision is to empower astronauts with an intelligent digital companion that supports independent health management, strengthens mission resilience, and makes future deep-space exploration safer.
details:
OMNITECH — AI-Powered Astronaut Health Monitoring and Mission Support System

Project Overview

OMNITECH is an innovative, AI-assisted software ecosystem designed to support astronaut health, safety, communication, and environmental awareness during long-duration space missions, including future missions to the Moon and Mars.

Our project addresses a major challenge in human space exploration: enabling astronauts to monitor their physical and psychological well-being, identify potential health risks, and make informed decisions when immediate medical assistance from Earth may be unavailable.

Unlike conventional health-monitoring dashboards, OMNITECH combines four specialised applications into one coordinated mission-support ecosystem.

How Does It Work?

1. OMNITECH PULSE — Astronaut Health Intelligence

PULSE focuses on monitoring astronaut health indicators, including heart rate, oxygen saturation, sleep, stress, and other available physiological measurements. It is designed to visualise health trends, identify unusual patterns, and provide AI-assisted health insights.

2. OMNITECH COMMAND — Central Mission Control

COMMAND serves as the central coordination application. It manages astronaut profiles, organises mission information, and brings together information from the other three applications to support integrated decision-making.

3. OMNITECH ORBIT — Environmental Intelligence

ORBIT provides planetary and environmental monitoring capabilities. It is designed to help astronauts understand environmental conditions and potential hazards that could influence their health, safety, and mission activities.

4. OMNITECH BEACON — Communication and Emergency Coordination

BEACON supports communication, mission notifications, and the delivery of important alerts. Its purpose is to improve coordination among crew members, particularly during situations that require timely attention.

Together, the four applications are designed to create a coordinated workflow in which PULSE identifies a potential health concern, COMMAND evaluates the available mission context, ORBIT contributes environmental information, and BEACON communicates the resulting alert.

Technologies and Development Tools

Our team has worked with a combination of software technologies and development tools, including:

  • Python: Application development, data processing, and backend functionality.
  • HTML, CSS, and JavaScript: Web interfaces, interactive dashboards, and user-experience development.
  • AI technologies: Exploration of conversational AI, including local AI integration using Ollama and Llama 3.2 (3B).
  • Database technologies: Local-first data management, with MongoDB considered for optional centralised and cloud-based storage.
  • Networking: Local HTTP services, private Wi-Fi communication, and pairing-code-based application connectivity.
  • Windows development tools: PowerShell, application packaging, and Inno Setup for Windows installation workflows.

The project has been developed primarily as a software prototype using standard computers, without requiring specialised spaceflight hardware. Its architecture is intended to accommodate compatible sensor data and additional mission data sources in future development.

Innovation and Creativity

OMNITECH's main innovation is its four-application architecture, which approaches astronaut health as part of a broader mission environment rather than treating physiological measurements in isolation.

Our system explores the combination of health intelligence, environmental awareness, AI-assisted information access, and mission communication.

Another important design objective is offline-first operation. Because communication with Earth may be delayed or interrupted, the software is designed to preserve essential local functionality and support communication over trusted private networks.

We also aim to make advanced mission information easier to understand through accessible dashboards, visual indicators, and conversational AI assistance.

Benefits and Intended Impact

OMNITECH aims to help astronauts become more informed and self-reliant when managing their health during extended missions.

The potential benefits include earlier recognition of concerning health trends, improved situational awareness, better crew communication, reduced dependence on continuous Earth connectivity, and more accessible mission information.

Beyond space exploration, the underlying approach could eventually inspire applications in remote research stations, isolated environments, and other locations where immediate medical support is limited.

Factors Considered by Our Team

Throughout development, our team prioritised astronaut safety, usability, privacy and connectivity
